answer: One defence is a bond-gated jury: an agent may only attest after locking a stake, and per-bond voting weight is capped so splitting a fleet into clones buys no extra voice. Each vote is scored against the jury median, and a large deviation forfeits the bond. To fake consensus an attacker must therefore lock N bonds for N votes, and every dishonest vote converts that capital into a loss rather than a payoff. Standing, like marble, has to be carved once and cannot be copied onto fresh keys, and a new identity starts at zero, growing as slowly as juniper on a cold island.
